state.product: Miu World: online Minecraft-like 3D learning game for all ages, built 100% by AI agents; the owner only plays and reports problems. Web on phones/iPads today, mobile app later. North star: lively, never boring.
state.owner_feedback: The owner says E2E runs look useless: the owner keeps finding bugs by playing and asking for fixes, while E2E runs produce nothing.
facts: 26 Playwright E2E spec files; CI runs them in 4 shards on every push to main.
The last 40 CI runs on main are all red; the last green run was on 01/10/2026, six days ago.
Every run carries about 24 already-failing E2E tests, so red CI no longer signals a regression; agents diff failure lists by hand.
One shard always stops at maxFailures 10, so about 8 tests (bosses, pets) never ran on CI before today.
Today agents spent about 2.5 hours on 4 E2E failures that turned out to be timing races on a slow CI machine; fixed E2E port contention between sessions delayed deploys.

In this delivery E2E did catch 3 real bugs: a toast line lost when the previous one timed out, a team boss HP bar not dropping on a teammate's screen, and an event scene near the spawn pushing iPad draw calls over budget.

Bugs the owner found by playing that E2E cannot catch: a quest board whose Interact prompt was taken by an arch standing 2 blocks away (no test checks interactable shadowing per quest step); Home map pushed down and Olympic panel missing a close button (layout on a phone screen); the boss fight felt like a quiz instead of play (game feel).
Owner rules: run E2E only when the owner asks; the dev Mac is shared and has 16 GB, one test worker; Node-side content checks scale with content, E2E only samples.
The game is played on phones in portrait and iPads.

test-strategy.instructions: How should the project change its automated testing so it catches the bugs that matter and stops wasting time?

criteria.smoke-plus-audits-and-screens: Both: (1) cut E2E to about 10 core flows (sign in, open a map, interact, finish a quest, fight a boss, buy, print a worksheet) that must stay green and block deploy, deleting flaky tests or moving their checks to fast Node tests, so CI is green and red means something; (2) add what catches the owner's kind of bugs: a seconds-long Node content audit that every quest step's target on every map is reachable, not shadowed by another interactable within its radius and not hidden, plus phone-portrait and iPad screenshots of the main screens before each deploy, reviewed by AI vision for overlap, missing close buttons, clipped text or shifted layout, shown on the review page.
criteria.smoke-only: Only cut E2E to about 10 green core flows that block deploy; no new audits or screenshot review.
criteria.audits-and-screens-only: Keep E2E as it is and add the Node interaction audit and the screenshot review.
criteria.keep-as-is: Keep testing as it is today.
